title: Somehow better than 15
body: I was a Gan tester for this product, and it is AMAZING. This cube has edge-to-center magnets, that have never been in a cube before. Because of them, this cube has insane auto alignment. The cube also has a new design for the edges, making it almost unpopable. You can loosen it a ton and it will still not pop. It is a great cube for all types of solvers. If you like a very fast cube, , this is the fastest in the world, because of how much you can loosen it without it coming apart use weak magnets too. Or, if you want a control cube, tighten it, and add stronger magnets. I have mine pretty loose, with medium magnets. I usually use Lunar, or Martian and Lunar for my cubes. This cube you can have so loose without coming apart I use Galaxy or maybe even a thicker lube. With Galaxy and it moderately loose, it becomes the most satisfying and smooth/fast amazing cube ever! All MoYu or Tornado lovers, it may be time to get a Gan. IT IS WORTH EVERY BUCK. (Even if I got mine for free). The tensions and magnetic rods are the same as the 15. The rods are the same colors, but have a white plastic covering the magnets, making them look better. It also has a very similar tool, except this one is white instead of clear dark blue. I like the blue better, but it does not really matter. It does make a clicking sound when turning though. Satisfying, but can get annoying after a couple hundred solves in one sitting. By far, best 3x3. Buy it.

title: The best GAN have to offer.
body: I own several GAN flagships and have tried all of their recent releases in store. I mained the GAN 12 for a couple months before switching to the WRM 11 upon it's release, however I always found the 12 incredibly pop prone. I also purchased and attempted to main the GAN 15 to little avail, I just found the cube too prone to pops, lockups, and very unsatisfying to use. I did try the 16 in store however I slept on it due to the obscene price tag and the fact the YJ Meta came with the same wing magnet feature. I was not expecting much when i first sat down with the V100, However I quickly found that even on the loosest tensions, which i prefer as i like my cubes as fast and flexible as possible the v100 simply refuses to pop, and rarely corner twists. The turning of the V100 is incredibly fast, almost to an overwhelming degree with a hint of tactile crunch, and the layers move with very little effort. This cube also auto aligns like CRAZY very similar to the 12, like this cube does NOT want to stay misaligned under any circumstance. The cube comes with the same adjustment system as the 16 while omitting the core magnet adjustment features. Which makes for an incredibly simple and easy setup process with very little option paralysis. I would absolutely put this on par with, and actually prefer it to the WRM 11 and Super Weilong V2, as the turning feels more tactile and speedy. The smaller size also makes this puzzle feel incredibly light and makes it an amazing contender for OH solving. Overall I am blown away by this puzzle's performance and value proposition and have moved into it faster than a Millennial father moving into a pair of crocs. For 40 dollars you really cannot get another GAN 3X3 With the same performance, and the black internals finally satisfy my wish of having a maglev GAN puzzle with black internals. This cube is easily my cube of the year and handily beats the performance of the V11 in my personal opinion. I do not think any of us were expecting GAN to come out with something like this, however some of the best things in life come at the most unexpected of times.

title: GAN 17 ... the BEST GAN Cube Ever Made.
body:
GAN 17 is the best GAN 3x3 ever made. If you already own a GAN 12 through 16, you don't necessarily “need” it, but you still may want to get it. I did, even though I own 12-16. And Honestly 16 is more then enough. But if you are deciding between the GAN 17 and any other GAN, GET the 17.  

 Pros: when set up properly with appropriate lubrications, it is buttery smooth, fast, more controllable than the previous 6 premium GANs, caps pop off easy, easy to adjust, premium feeling, and it snaps into place ("auto-alignment"), which is awesome. Plus, they kept the improvement to the 16 on the 17 with the UFO center shaped skirt.  

 Cons (or maybe not, depending): for those of us who like really fast cubes, this is probably the slowest GAN of all the "V"s (V12-V16). It doesn't have the adjustability options of the 14, the lightness of the 15, and the overall unboxing and packaging is basically the same. 

 What I learned from comparing GAN 12-16 to the 17, my conclusion is that by GAN adding all these magnets (more than any previous version), and the ball core, they added a ton of stability and control, BUT at the cost of speed and lightness. This trade-off will likely be well received overall by the community as I feel non-GAN users really don't like the "out of control" feeling of GANs, as well as some regular GAN users. Plus it's fast and light enough. Yes, it's still catchy and clacky, classic GAN, but it is an S or A tier cube.

title: Buckle up... its U5 Time
body:
This cube... is FAST... I main a GAN 12 on looser tensions with fast lubes for reference, and OH MY GOD... this cube is unwieldy even in my hands. I literally unboxed it... said "Can i get a U4"... and with one flick got a U4. After some Comet it helped add some friction between the tracks and gave it a bit more control, But OOTB this cube is a six sided fidget spinner. Turning feel is blocky and airy, feeling somewhere between a Gan 12 and a WRM 10, If you have ever tried or own a SuperWeilongV2 The hand feel is basically identical, although I would say the V11 is EVEN FASTER due to the lighter magnet strength and lack of adjustability.
 This cube is unlike any other, and would get 5 stars if it weren't for one, in my opinion Fatal flaw. The corner cutting on this puzzle... is AWFUL.... beyond 4 tensions forward gets VERY sketchy and struggles past 30 degrees, and FORGET ABOUT REVERSE. it will not even do line to line as the corner peice and center peice are both squared instead of rounded... Meaning the corner will just flat out catch on the center and it will not cut. At first i thought maybe i was just being unreasonable... but after seeing i was only set to tension 4, and my V10 Can make those cuts on the same tension with no problem, it is ABSOLUTELY an issue of design. You can visibly see where the Corner and Center catch on each other and the lack of any florian cuts on the center to allow it to cut those angles... Which is baffling to me because Moyu are known take that into consideration when designing a new puzzle and typically do not deliver this poor of performance. As a result I have found the cube to only be usable on the loosest tensions while using compression to dial it in. I am absolutely in love with this puzzle, and will be maining it for the foreseeable future. But i cannot in good conscience give this puzzle more than 3 stars for such a catastrophic flaw in adjustability, no modern 3x3 should be completely unable to cut 30 degrees on a tension above halfway, especially when those tensions are PRE PRESCRIBED and there is no  **** . If theres 8 tensions, give me 8 tensions, not 2 semi usable ones and 6 bad ones. Like i almost feel like this cube suffers from the same but opposite range issue as the Tornado V3, where some of the tension options just make no sense and hamper performance.
 This cube is definitely a main out of the box for me, however I would not buy it without trying it... I do not think this is as safe of a reccomendation as the V10 was and your milage will definitely vary especially with the 20 magnet version. I love fast cubes and can deal with blocky turning, so it works well for me. But this is definitely a release I would say you need to try before you buy. Hopefully v12 actually has 8 Usable and good tensions out of the box 🤷

title: Very good, almost as good as flagship mains
body:
I bought the Moyu RS3M V5 with ball core and UV out of curiousity. Regular price for the RS3M V5 is $24, but SCS had it on sale during Black Friday so I got this cube for $19. I performed 500 solves on this cube before posting this review. I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube twice. I have the cube set up on adjustment "1" (loosest), with the spring backed out about a half turn. 

 PROS
 Smooth and clacky during metronome exercises, getting progressively more clacky as the TPS increases. Corner cutting is excellent, and the cube really rewards fast turns. It will forward corner all the way past 45 degrees (50?), and backward cut at about 22 degrees at my settings. I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and Moyu's coating is as good as, if not better than Gan's. Removing the center caps is easy to do without tools.  The plastic feels nice and twisting is very forgiving. The price I paid for this cube represents a good value, with the regular price being about right. 

 CONS
 Adjusting spring tension requires a screwdriver (provided) and other tension adjustments require the provided tool. Magnets are not adjustable, though they are strong enough to provide indication they are working, both by feel and sound.  (There is no auto alignment effect.)  This adds to the already large amount of sound that comes from this cube when solving at speed.  It is a loud cube, from the plastic, to the corner cuts, to the magnets, there is a lot of sound such that solving this while people or watching TV, or in public, will reward you with a stink eye.  Finally, if you want this with a ball core and/or UV coating, the only option is to purchase it with the robot box.  The robot box makes a nice display piece, but is added cost without added performance. 

 VERDICT
 This is a very good cube, and if you can pick it up on sale, at a good price.  I don't find myself reaching for this cube as much as my mains due to the loudness.  The Guhong Pro is just as enjoyable to solve, but much quieter (and cheaper, though the Guhong Pro isn't available with UV coating while the RS3M V5 requires the package to include the robot box).  This cube isn't top tier, like a Gan 12, Gan 15, Tornado V3, or Moyu WRM V9, which I count as my mains, but it isn't much of a step down from those, either.  On my turning feel ranking, I currently have this (and the Guhong Pro) as 9s, vs. my mains which are 10s.  Although, considering price, perhaps it provides commensurate value if ultimate technology?  Considering AO100, this is very similar to my mains, so whereas I ranking it somewhere between 4 and 5 stars, I will round up from 4.5, though slightly below the Guhong Pro.

title: Great for synergistic purposes
body: At first when I got my Martian lube I used it primarily on a budget cube that was very clanking and a lot of friction among the pieces. I noticed it removed the friction of pieces rubbing against each other giving the grinding feel which improves the overall longevity of the cube. However it also made it more slower. Unless you have a super fast cube you need to combine this with lunar or stardust to get that fast smooth gliding effect. So if you are looking for a fast, buttery, controllable lube you need to definitely combine two or more different types to get that effect. Those looking for that buttery, controllable, but fast effect need to get either stardust or lunar and galaxy or nebula for that buttery and controlling effect. Depending on what you want to achieve. Lunar and galaxy is perfect for me in terms of speed control, and buttery. Sometimes I’ll add a little stardust on top to make it more speedy since it doesn’t last long and it goes away quickly if I don’t like the feel being too fast I don’t need to worry about cleaning it and starting over. For ultimate control and ultimate literally butter fell I’ll recommend nebula and stardust. Warning nebula will drastically slow down your cube exponentially making it slow but controlling so you need a super fast lube like stardust to counter it. All in all Martian is great for synergistic effects not so much as a stand alone lube unless you already like the way your cube is and just need to tweak a bit of control and cushion. title: Pretty, disappointing
body:
The Yuxin lustrous light-up cube was purchased to facilitate cubing in low light/dark, but fails as a speed cube. I pre-ordered this one instead of the shen shou lustrous because reviews stated the shen shou was hard to turn. The same applies to the Yuxin Lustrous.  

 Pros
 The lights and scenes are great. It has several nice colors and a few color scenes. The sticker colors are nice, and visible when the light is set to white. The magnets are strong and provide a nice click into position. Makes a good night light or desk piece.  

 Cons
 As usual with Yuxin, the cube is tensioned super tight and dry out of the box. (Seems tighter/drier even than the new plastic V1 YLM out of the box though.) The center caps are very difficult to remove, such that I didn't get two of them off for fear of breaking them.  But, there is no reason to remove the center caps since the cube tensions can't be adjusted. Unlike almost every other cube, the tensions are not adjustable, making this useless as a speed cube, or even as a practice cube for metronome exercises. When trying to solve, slowly, the light button (white center cap) changes the color scene in the middle of the solve at the slightest touch, turning the previously distinguishable color stickers to something not so distinguishable. 

 Verdict
 Great decoration, useless as a speed or practice cube.

I assume knowing that tensions are not adjustable (verified by SCS customer service) would be an important detail for any consumer considering purchase of this cube. title: 2 years later: Still amazing.
body:
Man, it's been a lot of history with this cube. 5.01, 4.86, 4.75, 4.69, 4.48. This thing has been through the world and back. But, despite its hype and the release of GAN cubes after this, the GAN 12 stays strong. 

 The performance is incredible as always. Out of the box, I guarantee you that IT WILL POP. It does not perform well without lube, just like your mo- 

 Adjustment is easy. My blue thing is set to 2, my clear thing is set to 3, and I use hexagonal magnets on the strongest setting, which still provides a smooth guiding feel without the CLUNK of the WRM V9. 

 Incidentally, I picked this cube over the V9 for that very reason. The beautiful quality of this cube is that regardless of how strong you set the magnets, it's never clicky. It flows incredibly well, and when turning fast, the magnets are not noticeable in feel but always helping stability. 

 Since this cube is too similar to the 11 and 13 onward, I'll be comparing it to my XS. 

 It's crunchier and not as quiet, but with my preferred lube setup (Compound X, DNM, and Mystic) it becomes nearly as quiet as my XS when they are setup identically. 

 They both cut very well, but the 12 feels more stable in small corner cuts than the XS, mostly due to the light weight and the loooooong core magnets. Notably, the XS suffers more than the 12 at very high angles, but who's cutting over 45 in a regular solve? 

 The 12 feels similar to the XS in the fact that it feels like you are turning absolutely nothing. They are both light, fast, and smooth, with no hint of resistance or sandiness. Of course, lube will change this, but it's worth noting. 

 The color shades are of course perfect, and the UV coating is VERY helpful with my hands being perpetually dry (I swear, my hands eat more Vaseline than a 2007-era Rubik's brand.) My only gripe is the lack of a stickered version still available, but hey, I own an SM, so that's cool. (I'm not selling it. EVER.) 

 The only downsides are the fact that it's pretty hard to get the setup right and that it's more prone to pops than the XS. For the setup, just follow my instructions and you should be okay, and the pops should be negligible. Honestly, I felt as if I just needed to say something at least a little negative so I don't feel like I'm blowing hot air. 

 Bottom line? Better than the 11. Better than the 13. Better than the 14. Better than the V9. I still love it.

title: Big. Heavy. Cumbersome. Tons of fun.
body:
Before this cube, the biggest in my collection was the Meilong 9, so I was excited to take on the 13. There were two popped pieces right out of the box (outermost center pieces), but I managed to finesse them back into place. Like other big Meilong cubes, the outer layers turn great, but the inner slices are a bit finicky and you have to be careful lining up all the layers before making perpendicular turns. I doused the 13 with Stardust before the first scramble, and by the time I had the centers solved, it was feeling a lot better. The solve was a great challenge, but man it's tiring. Had to take a couple breaks to rest my hands. It's big and heavy, so I relied on my desktop for much of the solve, but finishing it was a great feeling.  

 I've gotten spoiled with mangetic cubes and I was really missing that stability, but I can't imagine how heavy (and expensive) a magnetized 13 would be. For the price, I'm very happy with the product. Minus one star for the popped pieces out of the box, and just because there's still room for improvement in terms of overall stability.  

 Solve times:
 Centers ~ 1hr35m
 Edges ~ 25m
 CFOP ~ 2m
 Total time not including breaks 2:02:52! Much faster than I expected, but I can't help but think that I could have beat the 2 hr mark, and probably could have made it straight through without breaks.  

 Guess I have to solve it again...

The X-Man Tornado 3x3 V5 Pioneer is a premium flagship speedcube designed for serious cubers who want top-tier performance, deep customization, and cutting-edge technology. With magnetic positioning, MagLev tensioning, a 20-magnet ball-core system, and UV coating, it aims to deliver one of the fastest and most refined solving experiences currently available. 

 Out of the box, the cube feels quick, light, and highly responsive. The MagLev system replaces traditional springs with opposing magnets, reducing friction and giving turns a fast, effortless feel. Despite the speed, the ball-core magnetic system helps keep layers aligned, making the cube feel stable during aggressive turning. Many competitive solvers will appreciate how it balances raw speed with control. 

 One of the standout strengths of the V5 Pioneer is customization. Adjustable magnet strengths, elasticity, and axis distance settings allow users to tune the puzzle to match their turning style. Whether you prefer a loose and fast setup or a tighter, more controllable feel, the cube offers enough options to fine-tune extensively. 

 The UV-coated exterior adds a glossy finish that improves grip while helping resist scratches and wear. This makes the cube feel premium in hand and especially useful for longer sessions or sweaty hands. Corner-cutting is excellent, with smooth reverse cuts and very few lockups when properly adjusted. 

 The main downside is that advanced cubes like this can feel too fast or overly complex for beginners. Some early impressions also note that setup preference matters a lot—if left untuned, it may feel sluggish or overly soft depending on the solver. 

 Overall, the X-Man Tornado V5 Pioneer is an elite modern speedcube with premium features and excellent performance. It is best suited for intermediate to advanced cubers who enjoy customization and want a fast, stable, competition-ready 3x3 that can compete with the best on the market.

title: Gan releases another upgrade
body:
I bought the Gan 15 Maglev with UV coating as a potential main.  Regular price for the Gan 15 is $70, but I was able to pick it up during SCS Black Friday sale for $60.  I performed 500 solves on this cube before posting this review.  I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube once.  I have the cube set up on center travel adjustment "5", tension adjustment "5", with the green magnet rods (stronger). 

 PROS
 Smooth and quiet during metronome exercises, getting progressively more clacky as the TPS increases.  This cube is a bit quieter than the Gan 12 regarding magnet sounds, but louder regarding plastic sounds.  Twisting is easier, more airy, than the Gan 12.  Corner cutting is really good at speed, and the cube really rewards fast turns.  It will forward corner cut a little more 45 and backward cut up to about 22 degrees at my settings.  Corner cutting will improve with looser settings, but isn't necessary.  I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and Gan has one of the best coatings out there.  With the magnet rods I'm using, the click and 'bump' during turns is softer than the Gan 12 and the auto alignment isn't as strong, though still works from about 15 degrees with a slight nudge.  The plastic feels nice and twisting is very forgiving.  The price I paid for this cube represents a really good value, with the regular price being about right. 

 CONS
 Removing the center caps cannot be accomplished without the provided tool.  Adjustments can't be made without the provided tool.  Although there are three differents sets of magnet rods, the magnet strength on the corners isn't adjustable.  If I'm being picky, the plastic "clack" is louder than I prefer, although this is normal for high TPS on almost all cubes.  This isn't an issue unless I'm spamming solves while the family watches TV, or in public.  In those instances I'll select one of my quieter cubes. 

 VERDICT
 This is a great cube, and if you can pick it up on sale, at a really good price.  Although the turning feel is better than the Gan 12, I like the ability to adjust corner magnet strength on the Gan 12.  I typically set my cubes up looser, and deal with the instability in order to get better turning.  There is no reason for me to deal with loose settings on the Gan 15 since it turns great even at tighter tensions than I normally use.  Although, even at slightly looser tensions, the cube remains fairly stable, though it does get harder to control.  On it's own, I recommend this cube if you don't already have the Gan 12 since it is very enjoyable to twist.  I'm not certain it's an upgrade over the Gan 12, though.  There are aspects that are better (turning feel, slightly) but there are aspects that aren't.  I really enjoy using both of these cubes, and not surprisingly, my AO100 are very similar between the cubes.

title: A good, cheap smart cube?
body:
I bought the QiYi AI Smart Cube with UV coating after purchasing and using the Gan iCarry 2 for a few weeks.  I had wanted a smart cube to analyze my solves and wasn't happy with the catches I was experiencing with the iCarry 2, which caused me to slow down, making my solves non-representative of solves with my main cubes.  I pre-ordered the QiYi with UV for $25 as soon as it became available at SCS.  I performed at least 1,000 solves on this cube in the last two weeks before posting this review.  I purchased the SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube when needed.  I have the cube set up on tension "1". 

 PROS
 Smooth and quiet during metronome exercises or twisting up to about 2/3 speed.  At slow speeds and at rest, corner cutting is amazing at tension "1".  It will forward corner cut all the way until it starts to cut backward.  The UV coating gives a nice grip to my fingertips.  Removing the center caps and adjusting tensions is easy to perform without tools.  Each center under the caps is colored in transparent plastic to designate which side is which color since the cube needs to know the proper color of each side.  Magnets are semi-strong and provide a nice 'bump' during turns.  The plastic feels nice and twisting is forgiving up to a point.  The price for a Smart cube of this level is about right, perhaps even being a good value.  The app is very good.  Connecting the cube is seamless, and getting into practice sessions or 1V1 races is intuitively easy.  The analysis, statistics and replays are very well done and provide a great way to see where you might be losing time including adding up the total inspection time across all stages of the solve.  It analyzes several different solve methods, including Roux.  I've not yet had to replace the battery, which is supposed to have 100s of hours of life.  I definitely prefer this to having to recharge every hour! 

 CONS
 The cube gets significantly louder when pushing TPS, largely due to the catches when the turns aren't clean.  On my mains, I can feel the cube helping me carve the corners.  Although the corner cutting on this cube appears very good at slow speeds, it really doesn't like to be pushed fast with my turning style.  When pushing fast solves on algs that are very smooth, fast and effortless on any of my Gan 12, Gan 15, Moyu WRM V9, X-Man Tornado V3, or even Guhong Pro, causes frustration when soft locks and catches occur, taking me out of my rhythm.  My times using this cube are noticeably slower than my mains, largely because I slow down to try to keep the catches/locks from happening, which defeats the purpose of having a smart cube in the first place.  Finally, this cube isn't yet supported by Cubeast, although it is on CSTimer. 

 VERDICT
 As a speed cube alone, I would gauge this as mid, not even as good as the Guhong Pro, probably on the level of the Diansheng Solar S3M with maybe 2/5 stars?  If it didn't have additional technology, I probably would put it on the display shelf and rarely, if ever, touch it again.  As a smart cube though, it is pretty good up until you try to push the TPS.  Because it is a smart cube, the value proposition changes due to the technology required.   At the offered price, this lifts it up to somewhere between 3 and 4 stars.  Would I recommend it?  There are things I really like about it, and for someone that just enjoys solving at 2/3 speed, this is a pretty clean cube with a very nice app to go with it.  This is probably one of the highest value smart cubes on the market right now, but for ultimate twisting speed though, it still comes up short, but at this price point is probably the best smart cube right now.  I am rounding it down to 3 stars, so definitely above average for smart cubes, but not quite high enough to round up to 4.

Turning the cube by itself was fine, however the problems came when doing actual solves, as mentioned above. Even after lubing the cube and breaking it in, the cube did not get better. Out of the box, it was already awesome. Very little factory lube was in the cube, which made things much easier to customize, and the adjustment system, though derivative from its competitor, the RS2M Evo, was helpful. 

 The corner cutting was over 45 degrees forward and very generous reverse, more than the MGC. I would attribute this to the ball-core, but it makes such a minute difference that I feel as if it is just barely worth the extra couple bucks, adding a tiny bit of stability. The magnets are not too strong, not too weak, and since the two corner magnets are closer together than in the MS, it has less of that "bumpy" feel. 

 Pieces do not wobble around like they do on the M Pro 3x3 when turning, and stability is comparable to the YJ MGC Elite, second only to the Valk (we miss you, Valk 2.) Yet, with the adjustment system, flexibility is controllable and you can change between a little bit flexy to a brick (in a good way.) 

 I have no real problems with this cube, and I think that the only real issue is the dark green even though the difference in recognition is negligible unless cubing in low light. It's a good price, with good features, and is a great blank canvas for lube setup as well as having decent factory defaults. I highly recommend this cube for beginners and advanced solvers alike, and it is my choice over the RS2M Evo and the YJ MGC. I think it is worth the extra few dollars over the QiYi MS for this cube

title: This is a review
body:
Review: 

 Out of the box, this cube was not that impressive. That doesn't do much justice though, because almost every time I've gotten a new cube intended to replace my main, I liked my old main, that was set up, better than my new cube, out of the box. I immediately started playing with the settings to better the corner cutting. The first problem is that you can't actually get great corner cutting on this cube. The other problem is that corner twisting is easy. It took a while, but eventually, after adjusting the springs, screws, and magnets, lubing the core and pieces, and breaking it in, I actually got the performance pretty good. 

 Details: 

 Out of the box:
 Corner cutting:   Max: 1 piece(45˚)[bad]  At ease: 1/2 piece(22˚)[bad] 

 Corner twisting: easy[bad] 

 Feel: fast, dry, hollow, airy, tactile, bumpy 

 Reverse corner cutting:   Max: 2/3 piece(30˚)[good]  At ease: 2/3 piece(30˚)[good] 

 After setup:
 Corner cutting:   Max: 1 1/5 pieces(53˚)[pretty good]  At ease: 2/3 piece(30˚)[okay] 

 Corner twisting: moderately hard[good] 

 Feel: controllable, wet, hollow, airy, tactile, bumpy 

 Reverse corner cutting:   Max: 4/5 piece(36˚)[great]  At ease: 4/5 piece(36˚)[great] 

 Advice: 

 Do not take off the cap on the red, white, and blue corner (the corner with adjustable magnets in it) as sometimes the magnet adjustment mechanism can explode and you have to find the tiny little mechanism pieces and put them all back together in the cube. 

 Summary:  

 Overall I think this is a cube with good everything, however, there is a tiny gap left where the cube cannot corner cut. This is true on almost every cube, but since the reverse corner cutting is so good, and the regular corner cutting is bad, the gap is in an area that is more common to be corner cutting in, so you will get more lockups while solving. 

 I hope this review helped you :)

title: Light and effortless
body:
This is my first new cube since maybe 2021.  The best way I can describe this cube is that my fingers feel like they're pushing air.  Whereas other cubes I've had in the past (Tengyun v1, GAN 11 M, RS3M 2020 (reg+maglev)) all have some weight in turning (either due to friction or heavy magnets), this is the first cube I've ever used where I can turn as fast as I want and the cube doesn't get in the way.  The other cubes I've listed need to be loosened so much that they start deforming a lot, and even then they're not as effortless in turning. 

 It is absolutely great for  spam.  I use roux, so this is important to me and a reason I didn't like the GAN 11 M very much (the magnets made the M-slice take too much energy to turn).  The M slice glides with minimal resistance while maintaining stability and control.  Better than the Tengyun v1 in my opinion, as it is a MUCH lighter feel and doesn't really lock up like the Tengyun could.  It will also auto-align an overshot/undershot M-slice move back into place! 

 The cube needs to be lubed out of the box.  It felt very dry (plastic on plastic or "papery").  I don't follow all the special lubes that much, but some regular silicone weight 3 on a piece and the "triangle" end of a corner piece stalk was enough for me.

title: What a gorgeous cube
body:
I bought the Cyclone Boys Metallic 3x3 magnetic as a display piece. Regular price for the metallic 3x3 is $16.  SCS had the metallic 3x3 on sale during Black Friday and I was able to buy it for $12.  I performed 100 solves on this cube before posting this review. I've added Lunar lube once on initial setup, and am using the factory tensions. 

 PROS
 Scratchy, dry, sandy.  The magnets provide a satisfying "bump" to help align turns but not get in the way of initiating turns.  Corner cutting is okay, perhaps 22 degrees.  Backward cut is slightly less at about 15 degrees.  Corner cutting would probably be better at looser tensions, but this cube is used primarily to display.  Removing the center caps is easy without tools, but spring tension adjustments requires a screwdriver (not provided).  The metallic cube is absolutely GORGEOUS!!!  The price for this display piece represents a great value.  The plastic box in which it comes is a perfectly fine display frame as well. 

 CONS
 The metallic surface is slick, and attracts fingerprints (no kidding, lol).  The plastic feels "hollow".  Solving is not as rewarding as any of my mains, or even second tier cubes.  The colors are sometimes hard to distinguish, especially in places where reflections show up on the cubie faces. 

 VERDICT
 As a speed cube, this isn't great, perhaps a 6 or 7 out of 10.  However, that wasn't its purpose when I bought it, and let's be honest, looks trump usability when you have perfectly fine mains on the shelf next to it waiting to be twisted.  In fact, I am tempted to purchase six more of these to make force cubes out of them (without stickers, though).  Each of the colors would make a great unscrambleable cube, whether solid or patterned.  My rating of 5 stars is purely based off of its performance as a display piece.  As a speed cube, it would probably be at 3 stars.

title: A mid Gan smart cube
body:
I bought the Gan iCarry 2 with UV coating when I saw reviews that Gan had fixed some of the flaws from V1.  I had wanted a smart cube to analyze my solves but wanted a cube that was close in feel to my mains.  Regular price for the iCarry 2 is $50, but SCS had a killer Black Friday sale so I got this cube for $30.  I performed over 1000 solves on this cube using Cubeast before posting this review.  I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube when needed.  I have the cube set up on center travel "3" and tension "1" 

 PROS
 Smooth and quiet during metronome exercises or twisting up to about 4/5 speed.  At slow speeds and at rest, corner cutting is okay but not great at tension "1".  It will forward corner cut a little less than 45 (40?) and backward cut up to about 22 degrees.  I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and Gan has one of the best coatings out there.  Removing the center caps is easy to do without tools, though adjusting center travel and tensions does require a tool, such as the provided SIM ejector tool.  Each center under the caps has a colored retainer to designate which side is which color since the cube needs to know the proper color of each side.  Magnets are a little more aggressive than average, though not overly so, and they provide an audible 'bump' during turns.  The plastic feels nice and twisting is forgiving up to a point.  The price I paid for a Smart cube of this level is about right, perhaps even being a good value.  I've not yet had to replace the battery, which is supposed to have 100s of hours of life.  I definitely prefer this to having to recharge every hour! 

 CONS
 The cube gets significantly louder when pushing TPS, largely due to the catches when the turns aren't clean.  On my mains, I can feel the cube helping me carve the corners.  Although the corner cutting on this cube appears good enough at slow speeds, it really doesn't like to be pushed fast with my turning style.  When pushing fast solves on algs that are very smooth, fast and effortless on any of my Gan 12, Gan 15, Moyu WRM V9, X-Man Tornado V3, or even Guhong Pro, causes frustration when soft locks and catches occur, taking me out of my rhythm.  My times using this cube are noticeably slower than my mains, largely because I slow down to try to keep the catches/locks from happening, which defeats the purpose of having a smart cube in the first place.  The provided Gan app, Cubestation, is less than ideal and provides no additional value to the cube.  On top of the mess of a UI, it requires location be enabled on your phone, and other terms in the Terms and Conditions that shouldn't be necessary to play with a twisty toy.  Luckily, this cube is supported by both Cubeast and CSTimer, though it does take some work to get it connected. 

 VERDICT
 As a speed cube alone, I would gauge this as mid, not even as good as the Guhong Pro, probably on the level of the Diansheng Solar S3M with maybe 2/5 stars?  If it didn't have additional technology, I probably would put it on the display shelf and rarely, if ever, touch it again.  As a smart cube though, it is pretty good up until you try to push the TPS.  Because it is a smart cube, the value proposition changes due to the technology required.   At the sale price, this lifts it up to somewhere between 3 and 4 stars.  However, at the MSRP, the value drops back down since you're almost up to the Gan 12 UI by that point.  Would I recommend it?  There are things I really like about it, and for someone that just enjoys solving at 4/5 speed, this is a pretty clean cube.  For ultimate twisting speed though, it comes up short, especially at this price point.  In comparison, I prefer to twist with the new QiYi when I want to play with a smart cube.  It is an average cube, but I am rounding it down to 2 stars since it's not quite high enough to round up to 3.

Strengths:

 - UV coating helps with grip (plus shiny)

 - Surprisingly light and papery feel
 - Ball-core helps with stability
 - No adjustable magnets makes turn-feel consistent throughout 

 Weaknesses:
 - Though better than 56 mm, I think it is too close and causes me more fingertrick complications than the 54 mm Guhong
 - Weight distribution seems highly concentrated in the center ball-core (as expected), but this resulting papery feel is also something I am not used to and don't particularly enjoy
 - Need to glue to corner and edge split pieces together, or else they snap easily
 - Eats lube like crazy (good for a consistent feel during a competition though)
 - Rather loud (less enjoyable experience too) 

 Overall, the strengths definitely outweigh the weaknesses and this is an excellent OH cube with similar results to my main, the Guhong Pro M. It has slightly less enjoyable turning, but definitely a valuable purchase for anyone looking to get a budget OH cube that many also consider the best.

title: Amazing puzzle for A 11x11 MEGAMINX!
body: The biggest puzzle I had before this was a 9x9 and wanted another challenge. When I saw there was 25% off on this puzzle I immediately bought it. First impressions: TOTALLY WORTH IT. The stickerless shades are amazing (except for the 2 yellows, and the dark green and blue, in certain lighting they can be hard to distinguish). Everything else is really nice colors. You wouldn't expect for a megaminx of this size to turn well, or be very stable. While it is heavy, and locks up (obviously), it turns really well. I have had no pieces pop after 1 solve. The only 2 things that happened were a center piece would move under another center piece, but if you reversed that move, it would go back into place no problem. The other thing was that the "stickers" on the corner pieces got disconnected a couple times, but they get reattached really easily.  This is my first higher order megaminx puzzle, but solving it was very straight forward. As long as you know how to solve megaminx, and how to solve big cubes (4x4/5x5 or bigger), then you should easily be able to solve this puzzle, with maybe some intuition. Like I said I got this for 25% off (100 USD). If that offer is still up, I would definitely get this puzzle, it is definitely worth it. Even if it was normal price, I think I would still get it, but it would be a harder decision. If you have the money, like big cubes (technically dodecahedrons) and a challenge/ time consuming puzzles, I would 100% recommend this puzzle, it is amazing.

Moyu flagship, main worthy
body:
I bought the Moyu WRM V9 20-magnet ball core as a potential main. Regular price for the WRM V9 is $38. I performed 500 solves on this cube before posting this review. I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube once. I have the cube set up on adjustment "9" (loosest), with the spring backed out about a half turn. 

 PROS
 Smooth, clacky and quiet compared to the RS3M V5 during metronome exercises, getting progressively more clacky as the TPS increases. Corner cutting is excellent, and the cube really rewards fast turns. It will forward corner all the way past 45 degrees (55?), and backward cut at about 22 degrees at my settings. I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and Moyu's coating is as good as, if not better than Gan's. Removing the center caps is easy to do without tools.  The plastic feels very nice providing a muted sound, and twisting is very forgiving. The price I paid for this cube represents a good value for a flagship cube. 

 CONS
 Adjusting spring tension requires a screwdriver (provided) and other tension adjustments require the provided tool. Magnets are not adjustable, though they are strong enough to provide indication they are working.  There is very little auto alignment effect.  Being picky, the corner magnets may be too strong for my feel, causing pinky tricks to take a bit more effort.  Initiating turns on the WRM V9 takes more effort than on the Gan 12 or Gan 15. 

 VERDICT
 This is a very good cube.  I rotate this cube through about as often as my other mains (Gan 12, Gan 15, Tornado V3) and I find twisting it rewarding.  On my turning feel ranking, I currently have all my mains, including this one, as 10s, though this is "least great?" of my four mains.  All of my mains have very similar AO100 times, however, on algs that require pinky tricks, I have to concentrate to make sure I initiate the turn far enough.  I do prefer my Gan 12 or Gan 15 over this, but that is just feel thing, since I prefer light and fast over heavy and blocky.  This still easily earns five stars on its own merits.

title: Feels like an 11, 12, 13, and 14 combined
body:
- Has the weight similar to the 11.
 - Has the magnet positioning similar to the 12.
 - Has the dual-adjustments similar to the 13 and 14.
 - Has the center caps of the 14 Pro.
 - Lacks the adjustable magnets of all previous models besides the magnet rods. 

 Honestly the GAN 15 Maglev in terms of turning feel, feels similar to the 12 has most people say because of the positioning, but because of the spherical track design and corner feet, besides the magnetism, the cube itself feels...different. 

 It is so light so it is good for practice but in all honesty, I feel like the weight is not really an "innovation" and much preferred the adjustments like how we used to do it in the 12/14 but I guess this works anyways.  

 Going back to the performance, I don't know if I have a defective model, but my GAN 15 actually feels the tiniest bit scratchy from Maglev compared to the smoothness of the 12, 13, and 14. The auto-alignment when completing a turn is there but the self-alignment is nearly gone like the 13. Compared to the 12 and the 14 though, the 15 actually to me, catches. A LOT. Honestly feels a little jarring and interrupts the flow of the solve. GAN reduced the price in sacrifice of the adjustment features, but honestly with how this cube turned out, it seems like this was just very experimental and not worth the price.  

 Buy it if you have the money and want to try something less than 60 grams, but be warned of its performance.

title: Can't make every date.
body:
I was excited to find this because I have the 4x4 version of this with stickers but the stickers are getting worn. However, this new version is assembled in a way that makes it impossible to make certain dates. I found this out immediately when I tried to get today's date, 2 APR 2025. the R in APRV and the 5 in 2025 are part of the same piece so I can't make it say both APR and 2025 at the same time. There's no other 5 I can move into the place it needs to be besides the one on the R piece. After further examining, this issue also will occur for NOV in years ending in 2, and JUL in years ending with 6, for similar reasons. And MAR in years ending in 5 for the same reason as I ran into the APR issue that caused me to discover this.  

 Normally this would cause me to give this a 3 star review because I might be able to take it apart and put it back together in a way that will actually work.  

 But, on even further examination, there is no G at all on this cube which means I can't make any AUG dates.  

 Finally, the text on the DAY piece does not align with the first part (eg WEDNES, MON, etc.) 

 See the photos to see what I'm talking about in all of this review.  

 I'd really like a version of this stickerless cube that actually works for all dates and would give it 5 stars if the issues outlined in this review were fixed, because other than the major configuration issues, it seems like good quality. But all of these issues (easily avoidable) bring it down to one star.

title: Dream Cube🧡🧡🧡
body:
The reason I bought it
 -This is the most amazing cube ever! I have always been a huge gan fan but the cubes were always too expensive for me to buy any good ones. But the v100 changed everything. Its performance is good as a flagship cube and it's literally half the price. It having core magnets and being 55mm was just a perfect cube that I have been wanting for years. But if you add the shipping price it was still a bit too expensive. But when they released this CNY edition I thought God literally heard what I was saying. My favorite color is orange and it was a orange internal gan v100! So I bought it immediately👍
 The review
 -Out of the box its tension is on 8 and center travel is on 3. I personally thought it was almost perfect and I think most people would just use it without needing to adjust it because it is so perfect out of the box. But since I wanted to try everything I tried to set it as loose as possible and as tight as possible. And the most loose felt like it was going to crumble as a touch it but the tightest setting wasn't actually that bad. So for people who have light turning styles would have a lot more space to adjust their prefered set up. And because it is 55mm it was perfect for my hands since I have a bit smaller hand then others. I also liked the matte finish a lot since I have very sweaty hands. For those people who don't have a clue on what matte feels like it is more like a rubbery feeling than a sandy feel. And it's great👍 The core magnets are really nice too it doesn't punish you for not doing accurate turns. And since it's spring it is much more controllable and I prefer the spring for the v100 because it's already extremely fast and I don't think it needs to be even more fast with maglev. And my favorite part was obviously the colors. For people who like orange it's a must have. It's a very bright orange and the purple magnets don't really stand out too much so if you don't like purple it still doesn't matter because it doesn't pop out as much as the orange internals. And corner cutting is also not bad but not extremely good either at first. But after breaking in the corner cutting becomes better. And if you loosen your center travel to 3 and above corner cutting is great. But not as good on 1 and 2.
 Conclusion
 -Overall I will give this cube a 10000000000/10 it's AMAZING. What ever your thinking if you consider buying it even a little you should definitely buy it. It won't disappoint you at all and it will probably be better than you expected. And since gan said on there social media page that it's limited in quantity you should grab it fast😃

title: I love this cube, makes me want to practice!
body:
This cube is fantastic. It isn't the best cube as a speed cube, it feels a bit like an RS3M, but a little slower. 

 However, it's definitely good enough for beginners & intermediates+, and the App is what makes this cube amazing. 

 In practice mode, it gives you a scramble, and simulates inspection, and starts timing as soon as you start turning the cube, and time stops when the cube is solved. 

 The results can show you how much time you spent in each phase: Cross, F2L, OLL, PLL, and even AUF. 

 It also supports Roux and I forget the 3rd option; I don't think its ZZ, it's probably Petrus. 

 You can change this after the solve to see the results in different methods, or set it as a default in the settings (though I'm not sure if it works, I didn't try that). 

 My only complaint is you can't disable WCA inspection, so you only get 15 seconds to analyze the cube before starting the solve, otherwise it gives you +2/DNF.  

 It seems like there is an option to disable it, but either it doesn't work, I am doing something wrong, or it's doing something else. 

 It's translated from Chinese, but I didn't run into any major translation issues that hindered usability.  

 Especially for such a cheap price, this is probably the best tool you can buy if you want to improve your cubing from ~ 2 minutes to sub-20 seconds or beyond.

body:
The GAN i Carry 4 3x3 (Magnetic, UV Coated) – SSL Limited is one of the most impressive mid-range smart cubes currently available. It combines GAN’s signature smooth turning feel with Bluetooth tracking, CubeStation app connectivity, magnetic stability, and a premium UV-coated finish. For cubers who want training features without paying flagship smart cube prices, this is a standout option. 

 Out of the box, the cube feels fast, light, and very controllable. The turning is smoother and more refined than earlier i Carry models, with stronger overall performance that feels closer to a standard speedcube than many older smart cubes. The magnetic feel is balanced rather than aggressive, helping with alignment while keeping turns quick and fluid. Community impressions frequently describe it as a major upgrade over previous i Carry generations. 

 The biggest strength of the i Carry 4 is smart functionality. Through the CubeStation app, users can track times, analyze solves, learn algorithms, race online, and monitor turning stats. This makes it excellent for beginners improving fundamentals and experienced solvers wanting deeper training data. Bluetooth pairing is generally solid, though some users report occasional connection drops depending on device compatibility. 

 The SSL Limited version adds UV coating, which noticeably improves grip and gives the cube a glossy premium feel. Many cubers prefer this over GAN’s frosted plastic, especially during long sessions or humid conditions. The replaceable battery is another practical advantage, avoiding recharge downtime while offering long usage life. 

 The only downside is that it lacks some flagship smart-cube features such as gyro sensors, core magnets, or rechargeable internals found in pricier models like the GAN i4 or GAN 12 UI. If you want absolute top-tier hardware, those are stronger choices—but they cost significantly more. 

 Overall, the GAN i Carry 4 SSL Limited is one of the best affordable smart cubes available. It offers strong turning performance, useful training features, premium grip, and great value. For most cubers who want a smart cube without overspending, this is an easy recommendation.

title: Still the class of cubing
body:
I bought the Gan 12 Maglev with UV coating as a potential main.  Regular price for the Gan 12 is $59, but SCS had a fantastic sale so I got this cube for $40.  I performed 500 solves on this cube before posting this review.  I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube once.  I have the cube set up on travel adjustment "6", tension adjustment "5", magnet setting "3" (strongest), and the triangle magnet rods (weaker). 

 PROS
 Smooth and quiet during metronome exercises, getting progressively more clacky as the TPS increases.  Corner cutting is really good at speed, and the cube really rewards fast turns.  It will forward corner cut a little more 45 and backward cut up to about 22 degrees at my settings.  Corner cutting will improve with looser settings, but isn't necessary.  I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and Gan has one of the best coatings out there.  Removing the center caps is easy to do without tools, though adjusting center travel and tensions does require the provided tool.  Magnets are adjustable, and at the setting I'm using provides a satisfying click and 'bump' during turns, with auto alignment working from over 22 degrees with a slight nudge.  The plastic feels nice and twisting is very forgiving.  The price I paid for this cube represents a great value, with the regular price being about right. 

 CONS
 If I'm being picky, the magnets make an audible click that is louder than I prefer, although that can be mitigated by using the lower magnet strength settings. 

 VERDICT
 This is a great cube, and if you can pick it up on sale, at a great price.  It has been the class of the cubing world for a few years.  I typically set my cubes up looser, and deal with the instability in order to get better turning.  There is no reason for me to deal with loose settings on the Gan 12 since it turns great even at tighter tensions than I normally use.  Although, even at slightly looser tensions, the cube remains fairly stable, though it does get harder to control.  I highly recommend this cube, it is enjoyable to twist.

title: Fast outer layers. A worthy upgrade to the MGC line
body:
I was a little skeptical about whether the Speed-Micro Actuator version was worth it but after receiving the cube and doing a couple dozen solves I must say I'm impressed with the performance of this cube. It feels much like other MGC cubes but has a much smoother glide on the outside edges and it's slightly better on the inside. The setup was great out of the box but I may let the tension off a bit to bring it a little more in line with my other MGC cubes. 

 The SMA mostly effects the outer layer which makes the 3x3 part of the solve feel a lot more like a speed cube. It does feel like it speeds up the second layer a tiny bit but not nearly as much as the outer layer. On the 4x4 it's nice since all layers are beside a SMA but I doubt this slight speed gain to the second layer would translate to the third or deeper layer on larger cubes. That being said I wouldn't hesitate to purchase the SMA 5x5 when it releases. 

 Though still difficult this is the first cube larger than a 3x3 I've been able to successfully hit a 270° M-slice when doing algs such as U-perm which helps bring it more in line with how I'd solve a normal 3x3, especially using algs that only require a M2 which I can consistently hit with relative ease. It's also the first cube I've been able to perform a single action 2R2 when doing parity although the 2R2 is still quite difficult for me to nail consistently. I tend to undershoot it by about 20-30°.

title: My regret...
body:
It's a good cube for beginners but not really good for those who are trying to speed cube. The cube has 240 magnets which is triple track and the description is clearly flexing the cube with the magnet count. But to be honest because the cube is made as a budget cube and at the same time have that many magnets the quality of the cube is more lower than it should be. What I mean by this is that even if there are a lot of magnets you can't really feel them and the plastic feels like cheap plastic. It feels like they used up all the money of the cube just to add a lot of magnets and couldn't spend much on other stuffs like plastic quality and the actual turning of the cube. Speaking of turning the turning is not bad but extremely dry and I personally just don't like the feel. And even if the turning itself might not be as bad but the dryness makes it feel like it turns worse. The biggest problem about this cube is probably the lock ups. It locks up so frequently that It almost takes twice as much time to do 3x3 stage. But the inner pieces are not too bad. And I think the major reason for this is because of the cheap plastic again. It's also UV coated and I personally prefer matte and it just made it worse for me. This probably doesn't matter if you like UV. Overall I feel like Qiyi could have done so much better. Since it's a budget cube and is ment for beginners and not so much for pros it would have been much better if they just made it double or even single track and improved the actual material of the cube instead. A bit disappointed. But still great for beginners so still giving it 3 stars.
 And one important note to those who are buying any type of cube. If your buying a cube for the first time or only have cheap budget cubes(those who haven't used a high quality cube to be exact) it's okay to buy budget cubes again for your next cube because you won't know the feeling of high quality cubes and your turning style would be used to the budget ones. But for those who HAVE used high quality cubes before(like cubes over 40$ like gan cubes) and used them as mains before or still using them, I DON'T recommend trying out a budget cube and waste your money. I'm telling this because I just had this experience and don't want anyone else experiencing this again. I main the gan v100 3x3 and average about 18 seconds. I wanted to try 5x5 for the first time and thought since I'm a beginner at 5x5 and wanted to save a bit of money and bought the qiyi warrior 5x5. Since the gan v100 turning is extremely high quality compared to the qiyi warrior I had so much trouble with the cube and now I'm not doing 5x5 anymore. Because of this incident I don't like 5x5 anymore even if the 5x5 event did nothing wrong and it was just because of the cube. So when I wanted to try 4x4 instead I bought a high quality one. So the conclusion is to those who already know the feeling of high quality cubes, when you want to buy a new cube just save a bit more money to buy a good one👍

title: Very good
body:
I am a beginner (33s AO5, CFOP, 4LLL) and find that practice is easier with a smart cube. Was using the Moyu V10 AI previously and the Super Weilong V2 is a solid upgrade.  

 With tension & elasticity set to 3 and magnets set to strongest, this is significantly more controllable than the Moyu V10. My averages have come down a few seconds and solves have a really nice flow. 

 The largest improvement is how forgiving turning is on the Super Weilong V2; it really inspires confidence for those without perfect form. Connectivity is very similar to the V10 so apps like Cubeast work with the Super Weilong V2 AI.  

 Of course, this is a very expensive cube; there are better ways to spend the money if your goal is the fastest improvement in times (coaching, less-expensive flagship cubes, etc)  

 That said, wasn't sure if the difference would be noticeable for novices based on other reviews. My experience is that this is the fastest cube with controllability and is infinitely adjustable. Highly recommend if it falls within your budget.

title: What a cube, from QiYi X-Man Designs!
body:
I bought the X-Man Designs Tornado Pioneer V3 as a potential main. Regular price for the TV3 is $44.  SCS had the TV3 on sale during Black Friday and I was able to buy it for $35.  I performed 500 solves on this cube before posting this review. I purchased SuperNova service from SCS and have added Lunar lube once. I have the cube set up on axis adjustment "1" (tightest), spring tension "3" (default), and magnet force "1" (weakest). 

 PROS
 Smooth, smooth, smooth, and quiet!  There is just enough magnet attaction to keep my turns honest, but not get in the way of initiating turns.  Corner cutting is excellent, and the cube really rewards fast turns. It will forward corner all the way past 45 degrees (50?), and backward cut at about 15 degrees at my settings. Auto alignment occurs from about 15 degrees with slight initial press.  I prefer UV coating on stickerless cubes, and X-Man Design's coating is as good as Gan's. Removing the center caps, axis and spring tension are adjustments are all made without tools (though magnet adjustments requires a poky device, like the one provided).  The plastic feels very nice providing a muted sound, and twisting is very forgiving. The price I paid for this cube represents a great value for a flagship cube, and I find myself reaching for this (or the Guhong Pro) anytime I want to solve while the family is watching TV. 

 CONS
 Adjusting magnet force requires a tool (provided), though that likely will be played with over the first 100 solves and left alone after that.   

 VERDICT
 This is a great cube.  I rotate this cube through about as often as my other mains (Gan 12, Gan 15, Moyu WRM V9) and I find twisting it rewarding and satisfying, either solving or spamming algs.  On my turning feel ranking, I currently have all my mains, including this one, as 10s, with this at least as great as the Gans.  All of my mains have very similar AO100 times, even pinky tricks are satisfying since initiating turns takes little effort  (Not as airy as the Gan 15, but right where it needs to be.)  This easily earns five stars.

title: Expensive, but worth it
body:
I got a diansheng 10x10 with primary internals. It turns extremely well, in comparison to my meilong 9x9. Inside the box (new version) you get pull-out 2 shelves. On the top shelf you get the cube, and on the bottom you get accessories: cloth, screwdriver, stand, and giant cube bag(i was able to fit the 10x10, a pyraminx, a 2x2 with no problem at the same time). The box is nice and magnetic and not worth throwing away.
 Lets look at the cube. The cube is around 75 millimeters, and feels very easy to turn all layers on demand, although the middle layers are quite hard to turn, otherwithse, the 3x3 layers are amazing, and after break in, i was able to do the M U h perm with finger tricks. The 10x10 feels quite smooth, a big improvement over the cheap feel of the meilong series. The layers after break in feel almost the same. The magnets are the difference of a lifetime, though, which is one of the reasons to buy this 10x10.
 The cube hardly ever pops, so no problems with that.
 The cube is quite easy to hold with a glossy finish, and small. The plastic overall feels amazing and doesnt feel like a budget brand(because it isnt). The color shades are rich and dark and look better then colors on a meilong or other brands, the outer layer is slightly concaved, which, in my opinion adds to the feel of the premiumness. 
 In conclusion, this cube is a must have in the collection of anyone who likes big cubes, since non magnetic big cubes turn that audience away. I hope my review helps.
